Targeting Guide
Background:
Adora was brought to Etheria as a baby through a portal between dimensions, summoned by Light Hope, an artificial intelligence left behind by the ancient First Ones. Light Hope’s objective in bringing Adora to Etheria was to complete the mission the First Ones had tasked her with, a mission that required someone of the First Ones lineage to claim the lost Sword of Protection. It is for this reason that Adora, an infant First One, was brought to Etheria. The baby Adora was found by Lord Hordak, leader of the Horde, an army trying to dominate the planet of Etheria to serve his own machinations. Hordak brought Adora back to the Horde to bolster its strength after learning of the magical potential the baby possessed, and so Adora was raised to be a perfect soldier.

Years later, Adora was one of the best soldiers of the Horde, groomed perfectly by the second in command, Shadow Weaver, to take charge of the troops as Force Captain to finally win the war they were waging against the Princesses Rebellion. Along with her close friend Catra, Adora trained fiercely and dreamed of glory and greatness. However, things would change when one day Adora discovered an ancient blade abandoned in a clearing in the magical forests of Etheria. Upon touching the sword, Adora found her fate had changed, as she soon became aware of the villainy the Horde wrought on the people of Etheria and the power awakened within herself by the sword. Adora made the difficult choice to defect from the Horde and take on the mantle of She-Ra, wielder of the Sword of Protection, fighting for the Princess Alliance to liberate Etheria from the Horde. In doing so, Adora made an enemy of her old friend Catra, but found new friends in Glimmer and Bow, freedom fighters on the side of the Rebellion.

In the intervening time, Adora has trained in her new powers under the tutelage of Light Hope, Madame Razz, and the spellcasters of Bright Moon. She’s reformed the Princess Alliance and helped garner the support of the various princesses of Etheria, fought off attacks from Catra, the newest Force Captain of the Horde, and become closer to her friends Glimmer and Bow. Adora has discovered a life she’d never known in the Horde, one of laughter and excitement, of camaraderie and enjoyment, of friendship and fun, and she now uses the great gifts bestowed upon her as the Princess of Power to defend it.

Personality:
Adora is a brave, noble, and competitive warrior, true to her ideals and beliefs. She’s developed a strong sense of ethics since leaving the Horde and puts her all into doing what’s right, even when she lacks the wisdom or intelligence to effectively help. Adjusting to life outside the Horde has posed a great challenge to Adora. She’s used to strict schedules and absolute order, and so finds herself unsure and uncertain when given the freedom to act independently and spend time on herself. Additionally, she’s unused to many things considered mundane, such as sweets, games, animals, and family. However, Adora has developed a taste for these peaceful parts of life and thoroughly enjoys them whenever possible.

Adora can be clumsy and silly at times, with an evident lack of social skills and confidence in herself outside of combat. She also struggles with a martyr complex, being unable to ask for or accept help, and desperately trying to take on as many of others’ burdens as possible. She believes she is responsible for everyone’s well-being and places that responsibility squarely on her own shoulders.

Adora’s deepest struggle is discovering who she is outside of battle. She is uncomfortable being herself and doesn’t quite know who she is, who she’s supposed to be, or even who she wants to be. Adora is overly willing to set her own needs and wants aside for the sake of others, and has therefore repressed much of herself, hiding her softness and vulnerability from everyone. However, there is a burning passion within her that is easy to catch and will break free from the restraints she’s placed on herself when given the chance.

Targetable Qualities:
Heroism/Hero Complex
Military Upbringing
Child of War
Great paradigm shift leading to changing her entire system of beliefs
Loss of love and childhood, grief over the loss of her (girl)friend
Enjoyment of the mundane, love of life

Touchstones:
Gay gay homosexual gay
Chosen warrior of destiny
Fish out of water not used to new life
Learning how to people and what peace is like
